decisions.claim: B works in the same office as A
decisions.reason: 'our meeting' (turn 1), 'our secretary' (turn 9), and 'sent to the whole office' (turn 7) all presuppose B works in the same office as A.

decisions.claim: B shares a secretary with A
decisions.reason: 'our secretary' in turn 9 is a definite possessive presupposing B shares the secretary with A.

decisions.claim: B referenced a memo about a meeting to A
decisions.reason: A's 'What memo?' (turn 5) and 'The meeting was proponed?' (turn 3) are direct responses presupposing B referenced a memo about a postponed meeting.

decisions.claim: B is familiar with A's desk habits
decisions.reason: 'You know how things get piled up on my desk' (turn 7) presupposes B is familiar with A's desk habits.

decisions.claim: B told A that the meeting was postponed
decisions.reason: A's surprised 'The meeting was proponed?' (turn 3) presupposes B just informed A about the postponement.

decisions.claim: B mentioned a memo to A
decisions.reason: c6 ('B mentioned a memo') is a weaker projection of c3 ('B referenced a memo about a meeting to A'); c3 is the more complete claim.

decisions.claim: B claimed the memo was sent to the whole office
decisions.reason: Second-review support: A's question 'Are you sure it was sent to the whole office?' is a challenge directed at B's prior assertion. The interrogative form 'Are you sure X?' presupposes that X has been claimed by the addressee. A is not asking an open question about office-wide distribution; A is disputing B's stated certainty. This establishes that B claimed the memo was sent to the whole office.

decisions.claim: B suggested A might have missed the memo by not checking or not gossiping by the water cooler
decisions.reason: A's statement 'I'm usually too busy to take a bunch of coffee breaks and gossip by the water cooler' is A's own defense/rebuttal, not evidence of what B suggested. A is countering a possible implication but this doesn't establish B made that suggestion.
decisions.counterexample: A may be volunteering this information unprompted rather than responding to B's suggestion.

decisions.claim: B is a colleague in the same office as A
decisions.reason: c9 ('B is a colleague in the same office as A') is equivalent to c1 ('B works in the same office as A'). c1 is the more complete representative with richer evidence.

decisions.claim: B is not the secretary A would talk to about the memo
decisions.reason: A says 'I'll have to talk to our secretary about it' (turn 9) while addressing B, presupposing B is not the secretary A would consult.
